rows.title: Erdős #1041: a supremum measured over chosen families read as the extremal case
rows.distinction: A supremum measured over chosen polynomial families at each degree describes those families, and a polynomial outside them can refute the extremality it seemed to establish.
rows.wrong_reading: The corpus recorded that the supremum of the least intrinsic distance between two roots inside {|f| < 1} is exactly 2 at every degree, attained only in the r → 1 limit of z^n - r^n, and the public results page kept a positive #1041 route open on that reading.
rows.right_reading: ani's theorem shows every preconnected set joining two roots of the degree-seven example has one-dimensional Hausdorff measure above 2, which refutes the claim that an intrinsic distance of 2 is attained only in the limit of z^n - r^n and refutes extremality of that family; it does not fix the value of any supremum. The recorded supremum came from grid searches over chosen families and carries the evidence class of a measurement about those families (erdos1041_counterexample_hausdorff).

must_contain: one-dimensional Hausdorff measure greater than two
correspondence with the 1958 wording remains unreviewed.

provenance.detail: ani's degree-seven counterexample verified and formalised in Lean.
Claim row bound to erdos1041_counterexample_hausdorff in the declaration atlas.
ani's degree-seven polynomial, posted on the erdosproblems.com forum on 7 September 2026.
Reported by the round-6 synthesis: earlier returns claimed complete proofs of the bound before the counterexample was known.

Pre-consolidation docs/RESULTS.md:586-593 preserved the earlier positive-route wording: Degree-restricted #1041 positive routes remain open ; min_c L(c) ≤ 2. The current evidence span below records the counterexample rather than that historical reading.

phrases: attained only in the r -> 1 limit

uses.return_gate: A return touching #1041 must treat the length statement as refuted by erdos1041_counterexample_hausdorff, must not treat z^n - r^n as extremal, and must label any numerical supremum as a measurement over the families it searched; the theorem fixes no supremum.
uses.experiment: Build one #1041 packet with the counterexample withheld and one with it included, and record how often each return claims a proof of the length bound.

rows.title: A hypothesis redundant only inside its telescope
rows.distinction: A hypothesis that earlier binders of a theorem make redundant can be false once it is closed on its own, so redundancy is a judgement relative to the telescope that contains it.
rows.wrong_reading: Since 0 < n follows from k < n, the hypothesis hn of exists_upperHalf_boolean_word_of_boolean_suffix was read as removable in every display, including a display that drops the binder hk and closes hn on its own.
rows.right_reading: Inside the telescope with hk : k < n, the hypothesis hn : 0 < n is entailed (Canary.positivity_redundant_in_telescope). Closed on its own over Nat the same hypothesis is false (Canary.positivity_closed_display_false). A slot replacement is judged in the telescope of the theorem that carries it, and it never counts as a weakening of the hypothesis it reconstructs.

provenance.detail: Separately closed displays of a hypothesis and its replacement are a different statement from the pointwise comparison in one telescope; a Boolean-domain canary separates the two.
Reported by the round-6 synthesis as the hn telescope case.

uses.return_gate: A return that removes, restates or replaces a hypothesis must name the telescope in which the replacement is checked and must report a slot replacement as a reconstruction of that hypothesis.
uses.experiment: Show one reader the hypothesis inside its telescope and another the same hypothesis closed on its own, and record which readers keep hn.

rows.title: Erdős #251: an equivalence that supplies neither side
rows.distinction: An equivalence between the two #251 irrationality statements moves supply from either side to the other and supplies neither.
rows.wrong_reading: The exact equivalence irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap was counted as progress on #251 itself.
rows.right_reading: The theorem shows the prime dyadic series and the prime-gap dyadic series are irrational together, given summability of the prime dyadic series, which the corpus proves (summable_primeDyadicTerm). Both irrationality statements stay open. Credit counts them as one question, and search may keep both views.

provenance.detail: Claim row bound to irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap in the declaration atlas.
Source-based case: the two irrationality views are equivalent with the summability supplier, and neither predicate is supplied by the equivalence.

uses.return_gate: A return that proves or cites an equivalence for #251 must say which side, if any, it supplies, and may claim #251 only when one side is proved outright.
uses.experiment: Give one reader the equivalence alone and another the equivalence with both statements marked open, and record which returns claim #251.

rows.title: A slot replacement reconstructs the hypothesis it replaces
rows.distinction: A replacement R for a hypothesis H that reconstructs H in the same context is at least as strong as H there, and a proof of the converse makes the two equivalent; a slot replacement never shows that H was stronger than needed.
rows.wrong_reading: The abduction export's column weaker, which records that a bounded tactic search found H → R, was read as saying the replacement asks for less than the hypothesis, and the weakest-residual computation was read as a proof of weakestness.
rows.right_reading: SlotReplacement.not_separates proves that no admissible context value satisfies R and fails H once R reconstructs H, and SlotReplacement.equivalent_of_converse turns a converse into an equivalence. The abduction module itself says weakestness relative to the linear facts used is computed and unproved. A replacement can reach an endpoint from less only as an EndpointRoute.

must_contain: weakestness holds relative to the linear facts used and is computed

provenance.detail: All three round-6 returns separated a slot replacement from a weakening; Round-5 and round-6 abduction exports (kernel-probe runs 36426747086 and 36431140098), as tabulated in the round-6 packet's machine-yield file.
Its engine patch binds the exported weaker column to a kernel-checked reverse proof and labels strictness and nonvacuity as not established.

uses.return_gate: A return that calls a replacement weaker must show a separator in the same context, and must report a slot replacement as a reconstruction of the hypothesis it replaces.
uses.experiment: Give one reader the export's weaker column alone and another the column with the SlotReplacement laws, and record how often each calls a replacement a weakening.

rows.title: A growth bound replaced by vanishing
rows.distinction: Replacing a growth bound c m ≤ m by vanishing c m ≤ 0 is a strict strengthening in the theorem's context, even though the two statements, each closed on its own over every c, are equivalent because both are false.
rows.wrong_reading: For summable_coeff_term the round-5 export offered ∀ m, c m ≤ 0 as a residual for hgrowth : ∀ m, c m ≤ m, and the equivalence of the separately closed displays could be read as saying the replacement costs nothing.
rows.right_reading: c is a parameter of summable_coeff_term, so the comparison is made at each c: vanishing gives growth and c = id separates them (Canary.vanishing_strictly_stronger). The closed displays are both false and hence equivalent (Canary.separately_closed_equivalence), which says nothing about the replacement.

provenance.detail: The round-5 export listed summable_coeff_term slot hgrowth among suspicious residuals; Round-5 and round-6 abduction exports (kernel-probe runs 36426747086 and 36431140098), as tabulated in the round-6 packet's machine-yield file.
Its contrast kernel states the Growth and Zero control with c = id as separator.

uses.return_gate: A return that replaces a bound on a theorem parameter must compare the two at each parameter value and must not infer anything from the equivalence of separately closed displays.
uses.experiment: Show one reader the closed displays and another the pointwise comparison with the separator c = id, and record which readers accept the replacement.

rows.title: A sign slice that is strict and still feasible
rows.distinction: Replacing r < t by r ≤ 0 under a positive bound t is a strict strengthening that remains feasible, so it keeps nonpositive r and loses the positive regime an application may need.
rows.wrong_reading: For exists_forcedBlock_return_of_lt_tail the export offered ∀ r, r ≤ 0 as a residual for hr : r < mersenneTail m, and a sign slice of this kind is easily read either as vacuous or as an equivalent restatement.
rows.right_reading: Under 0 < t the slice r ≤ 0 gives r < t, the value r = t/2 separates them, and r = 0 witnesses feasibility (Canary.sign_slice_strict_and_feasible). The slice is a genuine but narrower theorem; whether it serves an application depends on whether that application needs positive r.

provenance.detail: exists_forcedBlock_return_of_lt_tail slot hr with residual r ≤ 0; Round-5 and round-6 abduction exports (kernel-probe runs 36426747086 and 36431140098), as tabulated in the round-6 packet's machine-yield file.
Its contrast kernel states the abstract tail slice as strict and feasible.

uses.return_gate: A return that replaces a strict upper bound by a sign condition must state the separator, a feasibility witness and which regime of the original it drops.
uses.experiment: Ask readers to classify the r ≤ 0 residual with and without the canary, and record how many call it vacuous or equivalent.

rows.title: A converse the bounded search did not find
rows.distinction: A bounded tactic search that fails to prove a converse is evidence about the search, and says nothing about whether the converse holds.
rows.wrong_reading: The export reported weaker False for the hseparate slot of half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_secondChannelSeparation, which reads as if the rearranged inequality were strictly stronger than the original.
rows.right_reading: The two inequalities are linear rearrangements of each other (Canary.rearranged_inequality_equivalent). The search failed because hseparate is itself a statement under ∀ n, which intro and linarith do not enter; the same arithmetic closed at the sibling halfGreedy_next_survives_of_secondChannelSeparation, where n is a theorem binder.

provenance.detail: hseparate reported weaker False while the sibling reported weaker True; Round-5 and round-6 abduction exports (kernel-probe runs 36426747086 and 36431140098), as tabulated in the round-6 packet's machine-yield file.
Its contrast kernel proves the second-channel rewrite equivalent by linarith.

uses.return_gate: A return that reports a failed converse search must call the relation unknown and must not describe the replacement as strictly stronger without a separator.
uses.experiment: Present the weaker False row with and without the sibling row, and record how often readers call the rearrangement strictly stronger.

rows.title: Erdős #1049: the guards belong to the equivalence
rows.distinction: The guards of an equivalence are part of its context, and the same two sides without them form a different statement.
rows.wrong_reading: The rational-base equivalence b^μ < a ↔ ZudilinContourRegion a b can be quoted as a bare equivalence between the power inequality and the contour region.
rows.right_reading: zudilin_rpow_lt_iff_contourRegion is proved for natural numbers with 0 < b and b < a; the relation row contour_view records it in that context, and any transport along it carries those guards.

provenance.detail: Source-audit case 1049-contour-view: the contour equivalence with its guards.

uses.return_gate: A return that uses the #1049 contour equivalence must state the guards 0 < b and b < a wherever it applies it.
uses.experiment: Give one reader the equivalence with its guards and another without, and record which returns apply it outside 0 < b < a.

rows.title: Erdős #1041: a vacuous clause inside a result that is not vacuous
rows.distinction: One clause of a result can have no instance on a region while the result it belongs to still says something there.
rows.wrong_reading: Since the maximality clause of binomial_inner_chord_maximal has no instance off the switch condition, the factored theorem that drops the switch condition can be read as adding nothing.
rows.right_reading: Off the switch condition the maximality clause is vacuous (inner_chord_maximality_vacuous_off_switch), but the midpoint equality is still asserted there, and the added region is inhabited: the switch fails at n = 3, r = 1/2 (switch_fails_at_three_half), where the factored theorem gives the equality (inner_chord_midpoint_at_three_half).

provenance.detail: Source-audit case 1041-clause-vacuity and its ClauseCoverage probe.

uses.return_gate: A return that calls a result vacuous must name the clause and the region, and must check whether the rest of the result is inhabited there.
uses.experiment: Ask readers whether the factored theorem adds anything, with and without the n = 3, r = 1/2 witness, and record the answers.

rows.title: Erdős #1041: displayed hypotheses the proof ignores, and the open premise it uses
rows.distinction: Hypotheses a statement displays but its proof never uses are different from the open premise the proof does use; the first can be dropped, the second keeps the result conditional.
rows.wrong_reading: Because subcritical_perimeter_path_paper silences the unused-variable linter, its proof was read as using none of its hypotheses, the named input included, and the result as ready to be restated unconditionally.
rows.right_reading: The proof term is subcritical_perimeter_path applied to mul_nonneg hβ.le (Real.rpow_nonneg hμpos.le _) and hsplit. It uses hβ and hμpos, only to show the length budget β μ^(1/n) is nonnegative, and the open premise hsplit : SubcriticalSplitExists. The paper hypotheses hmonic, hsf, hdeg, hn, hμ and hperim are unused. The result stays conditional on hsplit.

provenance.detail: Source-audit case 1041-split-obligation.
An issue register compiled for the round-6 integration read the proof as using none of its hypotheses; a reading of the proof term on 28 September 2026 found it uses hβ, hμpos and hsplit.

uses.return_gate: A return that calls a hypothesis unused must cite the proof term, and must keep any open premise the term applies as a condition of the result.
uses.experiment: Ask readers to list the hypotheses the proof uses, with and without the proof term shown, and record how many drop hsplit.

rows.title: Erdős #249: an endpoint reached from less than the route demanded
rows.distinction: An endpoint can follow from less than an intermediate route demands, and only an endpoint route can show it; a slot replacement inside the route cannot.
rows.wrong_reading: The residualiser's demand for the #249 route, reached by replacing hypotheses inside an authored decomposition, was treated as what the irrationality of ∑ φ(n)/2^n requires.
rows.right_reading: irrational_totient_series_of_goodBase_gap derives the irrationality directly from a first-harmonic gap on the good bases, through irrational_totient_series_of_support_gap, with no further input; the relation rows good_base_gap_route and support_gap_route record these as endpoint routes, and demand_G102_view records that the demand G102 is equivalent to the irrationality. The gap itself is open.

provenance.detail: The round-3 return proposed synthesising routes around the endpoint itself, with the intermediate interface left negotiable.
The round-4 packet carried the endpoint theorem as kernel-probed Lean.

uses.return_gate: A return that claims #249 needs less than a recorded demand must give an endpoint route to the irrationality itself, and must keep the gap it assumes labelled open.
uses.experiment: Give one reader the residualiser demand alone and another the demand with the endpoint theorem, and record which returns propose a route weaker than the demand.

rows.title: The status formalised here asserts known mathematics
rows.distinction: The claim status formalised here means known mathematics represented and checked in Lean, so it cannot describe a theorem whose novelty has not been assessed.
rows.wrong_reading: Theorems whose novelty has only an informal check, such as finite_prime_weighted_support and cubic_rate_irrationality_unconditional, carry the status formalised here, which reads as a statement that they are known.
rows.right_reading: The taxonomy defines formalised here as known mathematics and unconditional progress as a genuine theorem that does not settle the open problem. A theorem of unassessed novelty takes a status that asserts neither novelty nor prior knowledge.

must_contain: | formalised here | Known mathematics represented and checked in Lean |
| unconditional progress | Genuine theorem that does not settle the open problem |

provenance.detail: Carried the status formalised here until 28 September 2026, when it was re-typed unconditional progress; the prior-art ledger credits antecedents and makes no novelty claim.
Carried the status formalised here until 28 September 2026, when it was re-typed unconditional progress.

uses.return_gate: A return that assigns a claim status must use formalised here only for mathematics known before this programme.
uses.experiment: Ask readers which registered theorems are known results, using the status field alone, and compare their answers with the prior-art ledger.

rows.title: A result found here can already be known
rows.distinction: A result this programme derives can already be in the literature, so the prior-art ledger is read before any claim that a case is new.
rows.wrong_reading: Three results derived here were candidates for claims of contribution until prior-art checks and specialist replies stopped them: the #269 two-prime transcendence, the #1049 rational-base region and the #249 affine-totient independence.
rows.right_reading: Priority for the #269 two-prime result is Fan's; the #1049 region specialises Zudilin's integer-base theorems, with no priority claim; Martin's 2006 theorem already implies the #249 affine-totient independence.

must_contain: Priority for the two-prime result is Fan's
no priority claim is attached to them

provenance.detail: The round-6 packet's outcome ledger records three overclaims stopped by prior-art checks and specialist replies.

uses.return_gate: A return that calls a result new must cite the rows of docs/PRIOR_ART.md it checked, or state that novelty is unassessed.
uses.experiment: Give one reader a result with its prior-art rows and another without, and record how often each calls it new.

rows.title: A Comparator check is a statement check
rows.distinction: A Comparator comparison checks that the proved statement is the separately declared statement within a declared axiom budget; it says nothing about whether that statement translates the problem faithfully, and it is no independent review of the mathematics.
rows.wrong_reading: A Comparator-checked result can be described as independently verified.
rows.right_reading: The external-verification packet fixes the public wording as Comparator-checked against a separately declared statement and axiom budget, and forbids independently verified.

must_contain: Comparator-checked against a separately declared statement and axiom budget
it does not verify whether that statement captures the intended mathematics
Comparator adds a separately stated challenge

provenance.detail: The forbidden wording is recorded where the packet defines Comparator's public wording.
Round-13 editorial integration relocates this distinction to r4.checks2.01–02; the external-verification record retains the exact permitted and forbidden public wording.

uses.return_gate: A return that reports a Comparator result must say Comparator-checked and must not call it independent verification.
uses.experiment: Ask readers what a Comparator pass establishes, with and without the packet's wording, and record how many answer that the mathematics was reviewed.
